text:
aya: Quick flag from the nightly veridian-v2 q4 bring-up: we have a cluster of failures that look locale-specific (subtitle/vertical JA, zh ruby annotations, and several RTL punctuation reversals). overall BLEU delta for en->ja is -5.2 on the srt-subset.

sam: can you paste a short repro?

aya: pasted two small repros below (baseline float vs q4). these are direct model outputs from the run (pre-detok token sequence included).

aya: JA vertical subtitle sample:
SRC: \u300e\u7d42\u4e86\u300f
REF: "That's the end."
BASE-FLOAT: tokens: [TOK_10, TOK_257, TOK_99] -> "That's the end."
Q4: tokens: [TOK_10, TOK_257] -> "That's the end."  <-- missing TOK_99 and trailing punctuation moved to separate token sometimes shows as "That's the end ." or with stray \uFF3D (fullwidth bracket) appended. seen in ~86 samples where linebreak/vertical context present.

aya: ZH ruby (furigana-like) sample:
SRC: "漢字\uE010( pinyin )" (ruby inline)
REF: "kanji (pinyin)"
BASE-FLOAT OUT: "kanji (pinyin)"
Q4 OUT: "kanji(pinyin"  <-- missing space and closing parenthesis gets merged into previous token. token ids differ.

wei: thanks. did you check whether tokenization/merge table differs between float and q4 runs? we recently switched the quant path to use a reduced merge-table (q4-compact) and a generator tweak that prunes rare subwords.

haruto: I suspect the merge generator removed an explicit punctuation token for U+FF09 (fullwidth right parenthesis) and allowed it to be absorbed into preceding han/kana tokens under certain byte-level merge heuristics. that'd explain both missing tokens and punctuation stuck to words.

maria: any bidi examples? we saw earlier flipped brackets in another thread.

aya: yes AR example: SRC: "(هل ستأتي؟)" REF: "Will you come?"
BASE-FLOAT: "Will you come?"
Q4: ")Will you come?("  <-- ordering reversed in the raw token sequence (pre-detok shows RPAREN first).

sam: if the raw decoded token order changes then it's definitely model decoding difference or tokenizer feeding different ids. not render-only. can you dump token ids for that AR sample?

aya: AR ids: baseline: [LPAREN, AR_WORDS..., RPAREN] q4: [RPAREN, AR_WORDS..., LPAREN]. posted small dump to the GH issue.

wei: plan: 1) run tokenizer-only with q4 merge table against float model weights to isolate tokenizer vs model behavior. 2) bisect merge-table generator commits. 3) add locale-targeted smoke tests (vertical-srt, ruby, rtl-brackets) to quant-onboard.

haruto: I'll run step 1 now (float weights + q4 tokenizer). if that reproduces AR bracket flip then generator is the culprit. also will grep the generator history for any change affecting punctuation classes and ZWSP/ZWJ handling.

eval-bot: nightly-compact-run metadata: run_id=2026-04-02_02, samples=8k, flagged=102, top_flags=['ja-vertical-srt','zh-ruby-merge','ar-bracket-inversion']

wei: bisection update: narrowed to generator commits between 2026-03-25..2026-03-31. suspect patch "merge-prune-emoji-joiners" introduced a side-effect for punctuation merging.

sam: small sanity check: try running the float model with q4's tokenizer but forcing `--protect-punct` flag (we added a quick guard in tokenize.py but it wasn't enabled in generator). command: `python tools/eval_slice.py --model veridian-float --tokenizer q4-compact --slice ar-bracket --protect-punct`

aya: ran the protect-punct test: AR bracket order preserved when flag on; JA vertical punctuation also preserved. so tokenizer/merge table is the root cause. hotfix options: enable protect-punct by default in q4 generator, or revert the emoji-joiner prune patch.

haruto: minimal patch to generator landed as 9d1f0ac: enable punctuation protection for CJK + bidi ranges. will run quick regen and smoke evals.

wei: regen + smoke: running now on subset (200 samples).

eval-bot: 4760012560: regen-run-complete; flagged dropped 102 -> 2 (remaining are non-actionable stylistic differences).

aya: nice work. leaving GH issue open for follow-ups: add unit tests for ruby/vertical/rtl bracket cases, and a note in the quant-onboard checklist to run the `--protect-punct` path.

sam: also add a small integration test that runs float model with q4 tokenizer to catch tokenizer-only regressions early.

maria: please add a short postmortem blurb for eng-infra release notes so we can avoid rolling the generator without the guard in future.

aya: will do. tagging haruto/wei for follow-up.
